newsitem.title: USA: GKN could face total of $740 mln in damages.
newsitem.headline: GKN could face total of $740 mln in damages.

text.p: The British engineering company GKN Plc could face paying a total of $740 million in damages related a North Carolina lawsuit if a federal judge on Friday decides to treble the compensatory portion of the award, lawyers for the plaintiffs said on Monday.

In 1993, franchisees of GKN's Meineke Muffler car-repair unit sued GKN, Meineke and other individual and corporate defendants in a dispute over the use of Meinke advertising funds. On December 18, a North Carolina jury ruled in favor of the franchisees and awarded them $398 million.

That amount could run as high as $740 million, according to John Soroko, a lawyer with the New York law firm Duane, Morris & Heckscher representing the plaintiffs, if Judge Robert Potter decides to boost the compensatory damages to $591 million under the North Carolina Unfair Trade Practices Act, which carries a treble damages penalty.
Potter will assess the claim on Friday at the U.S. District Court for the Western District of North Carolina, located in Charlotte.
GKN has not yet paid any damages in the case. The company has about 564 pounds ($920.4 million) in cash reserves.

Officials from the company's U.S. unit were not immediately available to comment. An official at the company's London headquarters told Reuters earlier in the day the company had not heard about the higher claim.
GKN's shares closed up 12 pence at 997 pence in London trading Monday.
When GKN first announced the jury had ruled against it last December, it estimated its maximum exposure would be $554 million.
